purpose: Nine non-duplicative text/semantic checks for each of four figures: three research rounds with three deep-dive checks per round (36 checks total).
scope: Research overlay ONLY; no promotion to historical canon, SI laws, CQ/DQ formulas, engine mirror mapping or runtime.
decisionPolicy: Prefer source-observed default action over speculative motives. Keep narrative figure identity; cut unsupported behavioral equivalence and default labels. The word CUT here means deprecated as primary proposed semantic mapping, not deletion of historical record or runtime engine name.

profiles.sourceConfidence: HIGH for gatekeeper role; LOW for negative moralization

checks.name: Primary Dante action
checks.finding: Inferno III: Charon ferries the dead across Acheron and initially refuses the living Dante. His action is granting or denying passage, not his own inability to cross.

checks.name: Earlier classical action
checks.finding: Virgil, Aeneid VI: burial rites and the golden bough determine access; Charon also ferries those who qualify. Selective passage is a function of an established threshold.

checks.name: Internal Inferno consistency
checks.finding: Archived inferno:F01 uses THRESHOLD_GATEKEEPING and notes separate/protect/challenge as unapproved verb candidates; the figure is not assigned as a pathological condition.

checks.name: Repeated default movement
checks.finding: Across two primary traditions, repeated acts are selection, denial, and transport at a boundary. Core source behavior is GATEKEEPING; a shadow variant is unjust EXCLUSION.

checks.name: Motive vs behavior
checks.finding: The sources establish a role and conditions for passage; fear of vulnerability, perfectionism or endless preparation is not established as Charon's motive.

checks.name: Engine polarity stress test
checks.finding: ATUNED currently pairs Charon with Rumi's TR/Trust and gives him 'Threshold Paralysis'. A refusal to admit another is not the same action as failing to take one's own next step. The TR link is an existing design pair, not demonstrated behavioral equivalence.

researchRounds.focus: ADVERSARIAL GAP TEST AND CUT RULE

checks.name: Good-faith counterexample
checks.finding: Charon transports the properly qualified dead and responds to credentials. Neutral boundary protection cannot be automatically coded as decoherence; the harmful human pattern would require arbitrary, discriminatory or coercive exclusion.

checks.name: Alternative falsification
checks.finding: 'Threshold Paralysis' would require Charon repeatedly to postpone his own crossing because of doubt; the narrative instead has him operating the ferry. Evidence for the claimed equivalence does not appear.

checks.name: Cut decision
checks.finding: KEEP Charon as a literary Inferno figure with core GATEKEEPING. CUT 'Threshold Paralysis' as a source-backed default and SUSPEND any semantic equivalence to a human trust deficit; retain historical identity and the existing engine pole separately until a revised explicit polarity is approved.

profiles.sourceConfidence: HIGH for pursuit/retribution and Dante threat; LOW for doctrine rigidity

checks.name: Greek primary pattern
checks.finding: Aeschylus, Eumenides: the Erinyes relentlessly pursue Orestes to exact payment for blood crimes. Their function is avenging/retribution, not an automatic refusal to consider evidence.

checks.name: Dante scene
checks.finding: Inferno IX: the Furies threaten the travelers and summon Medusa to halt them. INTIMIDATION and threatened immobilization are directly observable in this scene.

checks.name: Internal Inferno consistency
checks.finding: Archived inferno:F06 identifies INTIMIDATION, and warns that they do not establish an equation between heterodox belief and pathological rigidity.

checks.name: Across-tradition default
checks.finding: Greek source role VENGEANCE/RETRIBUTION; Dante's local tactic is INTIMIDATION. VENGEANCE is the more general default, while coercive intimidation is a mode of expression.

checks.name: Trigger and expression
checks.finding: The Furies respond to perceived violations of blood and kinship obligations. Their obsessive pursuit and threats may bypass due process. This is different from holding a doctrinal belief.

checks.name: Engine polarity stress test
checks.finding: The existing RE Revelation mirror names Jesus and the Furies and calls the Furies 'ideological rigidity'. Vengeance might invert forgiveness/mercy, but does not logically invert revelation without a further owner-defined intermediary mechanism. This semantic mapping remains unproved.

researchRounds.focus: ADVERSARIAL GAP TEST AND CUT RULE

checks.name: Evidence opposing static rigidity
checks.finding: In Aeschylus' resolution the Furies ultimately accept an arrangement by Athena and become Eumenides, making 'incapable of updating a belief' a particularly poor global claim.

checks.name: Scholarly disagreement
checks.finding: The Princeton Dante commentary states that proposed allegories for the Furies and Medusa are diverse, with no consensus. 'Heresy' or 'hardened will' should not be promoted as the Furies' uncontroversial essence.

checks.name: Cut decision
checks.finding: KEEP Furies under VENGEANCE as the cross-tradition default and INTIMIDATION as Dante's tactic. CUT 'Ideological Rigidity' as a source-backed default and SUSPEND the semantic equivalence to Revelation's inverse, retaining the pre-existing symbolic engine mirror for separate owner review.

profiles.sourceConfidence: HIGH for narrative rebellion/stasis; MODERATE for model abstraction separation

checks.name: Primary poem evidence
checks.finding: Inferno XXXIV: Lucifer is immobilized in Cocytus; flapping wings reinforce the frozen lake; Judas, Brutus and Cassius are chewed. Stasis is an exhibited condition, not a complete account of an originating action.

checks.name: Narrative origin
checks.finding: In the Dante commentary and later Christian tradition Lucifer's rebellion against God precedes his fall. At the center of Hell he is separated from the highest love and unfree. The core narrative context is treachery and revolt.

checks.name: Internal Inferno consistency
checks.finding: Archived inferno:F11 explicitly distinguishes TREACHERY as the circle's category, STASIS as condition, and Lucifer as figure. They must not be collapsed into a behavioral diagnosis.

checks.name: Movement vs end-state
checks.finding: ATUNED's pre-existing engine text explicitly says Lucifer's pride cuts a person off from Source. That defines SEPARATION as the model's movement; Dante's frozen condition illustrates its end-state. Model claim and direct literary observation are distinct.

checks.name: Nearest source behavioral term
checks.finding: Rebellion/self-exaltation and severed relationship support self-SEPARATION; betrayal is Dante's location category, not an observed modern person trait. 'Stasis' is the feedback consequence, not the person's default choice.

checks.name: Engine polarity stress test
checks.finding: Jesus/Love vs Lucifer/SEPARATION is a coherent conceptual inversion within the owner's model of connection to Source. 'False Light' describes an optional technique for obtaining recognition; applause seeking is absent from Inferno XXXIV itself.

researchRounds.focus: ADVERSARIAL GAP TEST AND CUT RULE

checks.name: Historical text boundary
checks.finding: The 'Lucifer' morning-star vocabulary in Isaiah XIV originally addresses an arrogant king, and later angelic/Satanic readings are an interpretive tradition. Avoid pretending one stable historical figure story across all traditions.

checks.name: Adversarial false-positive check
checks.finding: Being unable to act, being depressed, traumatized or physically immobilized is NOT evidence of separation from Source, betrayal, or a Lucifer behavioral pattern; the moralized stasis inference is not allowed.

checks.name: Cut decision
checks.finding: KEEP conceptual core SEPARATION, with narrative trigger PRIDE/SELF-EXALTATION and Dante outcome STASIS; preserve the established Jesus/Love polarity as an explicit ATUNED construct. CUT 'False Light' as the primary/default textual behavior (may remain a distinct optional expression, not an asserted historical act).

profiles.sourceConfidence: HIGH for violent obstruction; CONDITIONAL for jealousy or possessiveness

checks.name: Primary act
checks.finding: Tobit 3:8: Sarah's seven husbands are killed before their marriages can be consummated. Repeated relationship-blocking harm is explicit; 'generic desire' alone does not describe this signature.

checks.name: Source motive variation
checks.finding: In Tobit 6:15 some textual witnesses say the demon loves Sarah; other Greek textual witnesses omit this. A motive of possessive love cannot be assumed as invariant across versions.

checks.name: Source resolution
checks.finding: Tobit 8:3 describes the demon's expulsion and confinement while Sarah and Tobiah's marriage proceeds, confirming the narrative obstruction's removal.

checks.name: Default movement
checks.finding: The lowest-inference shared source behavior is OBSTRUCTION, specifically repeated violent obstruction of intimacy/marriage. 'Possessive Obstruction' is a plausible compact two-word interpretation in versions that include the demon's attachment.

checks.name: Tradition separation
checks.finding: Encyclopaedia Iranica documents Aēšma as wrath/destructive force, with desire and lust related but distinct associations; later demonologies are not proof that craving is Asmodeus' direct behavioral default in Tobit.

checks.name: Engine polarity stress test
checks.finding: ATUNED pairs Asmodeus against Ramakrishna's devotion/surrender of desire under DE. Possessive obstruction is a useful *hypothetical* grasping-vs-surrender contrast, but is not independently established as one-to-one by Tobit.

researchRounds.focus: ADVERSARIAL GAP TEST AND CUT RULE

checks.name: Discriminating act from emotional intensity
checks.finding: Healthy desire or consensual pleasure is not the adverse behavior. The differentiator is destructive interference with others' safety and agency, not the fact of wanting.

checks.name: Alternative motive falsification
checks.finding: Jealousy, coercive possessiveness, rage and lust are interpretive alternatives, not equally evidenced motives. The narrative act persists even if one removes all motives: partners are harmed and union blocked.

checks.name: Cut decision
checks.finding: KEEP source core OBSTRUCTION (more precisely RELATIONAL OBSTRUCTION). Retain 'Possessive Obstruction' only as a version-dependent behavioral reading and DE pole mapping as an ATUNED model candidate. CUT 'Compulsive Craving' as the asserted primary story behavior; a later lust-related tradition may remain a clearly different secondary association.

notes: Charon and Furies do have source figure behaviors; it is their existing behavioral-equivalence labels that fail close source matching.
Lucifer's Separation is an ATUNED layer abstraction supported by its own engine definition; do not claim the Inferno text uses that exact diagnostic term.
Asmodeus' claimed possessive motive is text-variant sensitive. Obstruction remains the least inference-heavy label.
A true runtime change requires a separate audited join migration, which is deliberately not included.
